title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
The page sets up a lattice-theoretic classification of real elliptic curves. It serves the 'chirurgie des surfaces conformes' project, which handles surfaces with real structure, Klein surfaces, boundaries and non-orientable surfaces through anti-holomorphic involutions.

(1) A real elliptic curve, up to isomorphism, is encoded by an 'R-system' (Π, σ, c):
- Π ≅ Z^2 is the period lattice H_1.
- c is an oriented conformal structure on Π_R = Π⊗R, i.e. a complex structure making Π_R ≅ C, so that X = Π_R/Π.
- σ is an anti-automorphism of (Π, c): an involution of Π of determinant −1 (hence ≠ ±id). It reverses the orientation and preserves the underlying unoriented conformal structure. It is the action of complex conjugation on H_1.

(2) The pair (Π, σ) has exactly two isomorphism types. These are the Z[Z/2]-lattices of rank 2 whose eigenvalues are +1 and −1. The previous page computes them via M_+ ⊕ M_− ⊂ M ⊂ ½(M_+ ⊕ M_−) and subgroups m ⊂ P/2P × Q/2Q.
- Split type: Π = Π_+ ⊕ Π_−, σ = diag(1, −1). This is the rectangular lattice, with two real components.
- Non-split type: σ swaps the basis vectors, and Π_+ ⊕ Π_− has index 2 in Π. This is the rhombic lattice, with one real component.
Grothendieck notes the two types are isogenous; indeed there is a 2-isogeny between them.

(3) A σ-invariant conformal structure is a positive quadratic form Q, up to scaling, for which Π_+ and Π_− are orthogonal. Normalizing Q(e_+) = 1 gives Q(x e_+ + y e_−) = x^2 + a y^2 with a > 0. This yields two families E_a (split) and E'_a (non-split), each parametrized by R_{>0}. In modern terms this is the classical description of the real points of the moduli of elliptic curves:
- rectangular lattices Z + i t Z, with a = t^2, cover j ≥ 1728 (Δ > 0);
- rhombic lattices cover j ≤ 1728 (Δ < 0).
The values a and 1/a give the two quadratic twists by −1 with the same real j. For example, at j = 1728 the two families meet the square lattice in two different real forms, y^2 = x^3 − x and y^2 = x^3 + x.

(4) Automorphisms of the real curve (fixing the origin) are lattice automorphisms that commute with σ and preserve the oriented conformal structure. Such a map preserves Π_+ and Π_−, so it acts by ±1 on e_+ and on e_−. The orientation constraint then leaves only id and −id. The conclusion is that the automorphism group of every real elliptic curve is {±1}, generated by the 'universal' automorphism −id_Π.

The next page reverses the viewpoint. Fix a complex curve and let G be the group of lattice automorphisms preserving the unoriented conformal structure. Real structures exist iff det: G → {±1} is onto, and G is then dihedral.
errors: No real mathematical errors. The phrase 'structures conformes invariantes par σ' must mean the unoriented conformal structure (σ reverses the orientation of c), which is how it is used.

Grothendieck does not remark that E_a and E_{1/a} (likewise E'_a and E'_{1/a}) have isomorphic complexifications; they are the two real forms (twists by −1) of one complex curve. This is not an error, since the parametrization of real isomorphism classes by a ∈ R_{>0} is injective. The next page takes up exactly this question.

ideas.what: Real elliptic curves encoded as (lattice, orientation-reversing involution, σ-invariant conformal structure)
ideas.modern_name: Real structures on complex tori via anti-holomorphic involutions on H_1; Klein-surface description of real elliptic curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein; Weichold; Alling–Greenleaf on Klein surfaces 1971; Silhol, Real Algebraic Surfaces 1989)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions extending to surfaces with boundary and non-orientable surfaces and the role of complex conjugation, but not this computation

ideas.what: Exactly two isomorphism types of (Z^2, involution of det −1): split versus non-split, which are 2-isogenous
ideas.modern_name: Indecomposable integral representations of Z/2 of rank 2; rectangular vs rhombic lattices; real elliptic curves with Δ>0 vs Δ<0
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Reiner on integral representations of cyclic groups of prime order; classical theory of real elliptic functions)

ideas.what: Moduli of real elliptic curves as two copies of R_{>0} (Q = x^2 + a y^2)
ideas.modern_name: Real locus of the modular curve / moduli of real elliptic curves (Seppälä–Silhol)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; Seppälä–Silhol (1989) for real moduli in general

ideas.what: The automorphism group of a real elliptic curve with origin is {±1}

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean, correct re-derivation of the classical classification of real elliptic curves (rectangular vs rhombic lattices, two half-line families, automorphism group ±1). It is a working computation inside the conformal-surgery project, with nothing new relative to the literature.

The insertion above line 6 reads roughly 'une invol. de Π⊗R i.e. de déterminant −1'. The main line reads 'qui peut s'interpréter comme une involution de Π, renversant l'orientation (donc ≠ ±id_Π)'.
